questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Somewhere with nature and focus on sustainablity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been costly, but was woth it in the end. University of Auckland made everything very easy, but the University of Copenhagen made the process a bit hard. I think they could da a lot to improve their support for students who plan to go on exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was picked up in the airport and recieved a totebag with a short-term simcard for my phone as well. They drove me all the way to the door and made sure i was recieved at the accommodation even though it was night time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: i could prioritize different types of housing

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: there was none on the housing i choose, but it did not want a meal plan. I had all the cooking facilities avaible so i could cook dinners myself. I Lived ad Stanley.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Stanley and Nicholls is really nice if you want the apartment vibe. I think they paired us by age, which was very nice. It's very expensive but i would not change it for the world. They are very strict with different rules - you don't have as much freedom as you do in an apartment in europe. But it was fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It could be cheaper.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: hh

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was pretty tricky to figure out what courses i could actually enrol to and also which ones needed concession approval. It did not seem like there was a real system to this, but seemed rather random. It was a bit frusturating, but i ended up getting enrolled to some really nice courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the help desk was very helpfull and answered very fast.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesful but after a rather chaotic process of enrolling to a bunch of classes just to make sure i was accepted to some.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would make sure to check the level of the classes. the univeristy of copenhagen was very harsh on what level the classes should be at, even though other universities are more chill about it. Start looking into  courses early - some get filled up pretty quickly, so you have to be ready. But you can also pick and choose even after you arrive to the country, so don't stress too much about it. I choose courses  where I only had to attend classes from monday to wednesday, which gave me two full days of the week to study or travel. That was amazing. Can recommend looking into the schedule of the courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I learned so much, but we had a lot of assignments, so that took up some time.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: all 700+. I had to write many assignments and do severel tests thorughut the semester which was very different from back home. But I also learned a lot and many other students had similar workloads. Would look into what kind of exam your courses have before choosing.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was lucky that I had a lot of small classes, meaning we could discuss many of the topics. It was very similar to home expect the heavy load on assignments and tests throughout the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: GEOG738, GEOG725, GEOG750, POLI770

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: all of them! They were great.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The living costs are just way higher in New Zealand than to back home. This surprised me a lot. Flight tickets were also more expensive than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Almost everything was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have so many clubs you can join and people are super engaged!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Climbing, Hiking was what i joined. But there was a club for everything you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Climbing and hiking.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go anywhere that's not auckland! Spend all the time you can on checking out New Zealand. There is so many beautiful places both on the north and the south island. Some people bought a car and have earned money on selling them before leaving. We rented cars and that was so fine when we split the costs. bring hiking gear and camping gear if you're into that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: get a mullet.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was more "american" than I though. Car culture. But also very communal apporach to many things. Way more inclusive in their approach to different people. Also more religious outside of Auckalnd than expected.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The communal and open approach to LGBTQ+ and other minorities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Prioritize Stanley as the highest for uni housing
2) Try to get courses you find interesting but where the workload isn't to heavy 
3) Use your freetime wisely and see nature! Join the clubs!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's expensive, so apply for scholarships!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All of the friends and nature experiences.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The very heavy workload I had from my courses on master's level. It's not as bad on bacherlor's.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
